signature: On bell: "MACHT. ANTONI. SCHNICZER. ZV. NVRNBERG [crown] M.D.LXXVIIII".
mouthpiece: original; ext. diam. 23.7, depth of bowl 17.9, throat 8.2.²   ; inscription: "NVRMBERG."
dimensions: Diam. of mouthpipe opening 9, bo 10.5, be 98, le 3505, h 1090.
provenance: Purchased in 1590 by the Accademia Filarmonica from Count Giordano Serego, “valente virtuoso dello strumento,״ for 15 corone d'oro, with funds from the sale of some viols.³   An inventory of the Accademia Filarmonica from 1562 mentions “un trombone de laton fornido delli suoi pezzi.”
literature: Paganuzzi et al. 1976: 156 (photo); Archivio del Accademia Filarmonica di Verona, Reg. n. 30;⁴  Jahn 1925; Langwill 1980: 159; Van der Meer & Weber 1982: 72–74, 128 (photo); Paganuzzi 1987: 24–29 (photo); SmithD 1989: 32; Waterhouse 1993: 360; McGowan 1996: 90–101; Guion 2010: 19; Carter 2012: 293, 295, 297–98 (photos); Vereecke 2011: 25–41; Vereecke 2016: ****.
remarks: Ring in slide-bow; two coils of tubing in bell sec.; ball in bell-pipe in manner of trumpet; facsimile in US-NY (Crosby Brown, #2561); ring in slide-bow and in one of the coils; flat slide-stays with geometric ornaments; sleeve at top of moveable slide-stay has medallion with figure of shawm and lute; immoveable slide-stay apparently a modern replacement;⁵   dragon-head clasps with eyelets on slide-stays. Flat bell-stay, apparently a modern replacement.⁶   Bell has only modest terminal flare. The 19 ferrules, moveable slide-stay and adjacent sleeves, the heads of the pins for the hinges on the flat slide-stays, three saddles, and the rim wire of the bell are gold-plated; the dragon-head clasps and the medallion on the sleeve of the moveable slide-stay are silver-plated. Extra crooks and tuning bits; see McGowan 1996, who talks about “two extra slide tubes;” can be extended to form a Sekund- or even a Terz-posaun (i.e., pitched either a second or a third below a tenor in A). Examined by Carter, March 2001.
footnotes: According to Van der Meer & Weber (1982: 74) "Fondamentale Fa0# (probabilmente un Fa0 alto)" (trans.: probably in F at high pitch). This seems unlikely, as there is no evidence that bass trombones were built in F at this early date.
